Pod Rundown

—

Ratings

Scored from card tags (rules 0.10.19, pre-release). Each stat aims for 10, the mark of a strong deck. Engine, Offense and Defense are each out of 30, so the total is out of 90; points above 10 count half in the totals. Click a column to sort (on a phone, tap a deck to open it).

1–4Low 5–8Medium 9–10High 10+Over the mark · Salt 🟦 0–10 🟩 11–20 🟨 21–30 🟧 31–40 🟥 41+ · Cheez = 🧀 Cheese Wedge · Leon = 🪼 Jellyfish

Decks

Pick a deck by name. Each one has its stat graph, a Takeaway tab and a tab for every stat; the dashed ring on the graph is 10. You can also click a deck's name in the ratings table.

Garage

Pick a deck like picking a car. Each bar has 15 blocks; the dashed block is 10 (a strong deck), orange blocks are over 10, red bars are 4 or less, and the blue line is the pod average.

Stat Breakdown

Pick a stat: what it measures, the exact card formulas, the deck-level checks, how the rating is worked out, and where every deck stands. Click a deck to open it.

The Crypt

Pick a player: spin their haunted deck wheel to choose what they play next, read up on how they play, flip a coin or roll the bones.

Pod Sim

Pick four different decks (or roll the dice) and press play. Every possible pod of four was played 100 times with the real decklists; each game shows one of that pod's common outcomes (more likely the more often it happened), told as an early-game and mid-game rundown and then the turns where players fall. The same pod can end differently each time you press play.

What's new

📱 Sideways on phones, a bigger-faced life tracker, and longer stages

  • Crypt Crawl and the life tracker now snap sideways on a phone held upright, filling the screen in landscape (⟳ toggles it). The ⛶ button uses real full screen where the browser allows it (Android) and falls back to the sideways view (iPhone).
  • Life tracker: each panel has its buttons stacked on the left (+5, +1, −1, −5), the name with the life total under it, and the status-bar face filling the rest of the panel. The who-goes-first cards use the classic card back.
  • Crypt Crawl stages last about twice as long (about twice the monsters), each worth about half the XP. The Geode Golem now opens with Seismic Slam, a melee shockwave.

💰 Crypt Crawl: gold, gear score, a boss-time merchant, and a smarter battlefield

  • Gold: monsters sometimes drop gold piles your party scoops up as it walks over them (elites always, bosses a big pile). Gold belongs to the save and is kept even when a run ends.
  • Items no longer come from level-ups (those are skills only). They drop rarely: basic monsters only up to Uncommon, elites up to Rare, bosses always drop one; odds improve the deeper you go. After every boss win a 🛒 Merchant sets up at camp with better stock (Uncommon or better, a good shot at Rare, Legendary once unlocked), plus restocking and honing (+1 rank). Spare items in the backpack can be sold.
  • Gear Score: every item shows a GS from its rank and how deep it was found (deeper items are a little stronger); each hero shows their Gear total at camp.
  • Positions: ranged heroes stand 2/10 across the screen, melee heroes 4/10, ranged summons 5/10, melee summons 7/10.
  • Summons now swing and shoot with real attack animations, flash when hit, show a small health bar, and take damage: melee monsters attack whatever summon is in their way when no hero is close, and some flyers go after summons.
  • Flankers: hounds, wolfmen, ghouls and spiders try to slip past the front line and attack your ranged heroes; melee heroes can turn on monsters behind them and ranged heroes shoot backwards.

⭐ Crypt Crawl: the stranger or a blessing

  • Every run that clears stage 6 with fewer than 3 heroes meets the mystery stranger: take them into the party, or leave them be for a ⭐ Blessed Upgrade (each option is Uncommon or better, about a 40% shot at Rare each). Leaving them is permanent for that save: it stays a 2-hero party, and later runs that clear stage 6 get the blessing again. Players with no other heroes to add get the blessing automatically (and can still take a third hero later once they have one). Every save, new or old, starts at 2 heroes; the third spot opens only when you save the stranger.

⚠️ Crypt Crawl: telegraphed boss attacks, Reflex, and livelier heroes

  • Heroes shuffle around on their own like a beat-'em-up (more while standing and fighting), which can carry them clear of danger by luck.
  • Big boss moves now mark the ground first with a pulsing zone: the Gravelord's Grave Slam (green), the Countess's Blood Rain (red, two spots) and the Maw's tentacles (purple). Whoever is still inside when it lands takes the hit.
  • New hero stat Reflex (REF on the hero cards): the chance to notice a marked zone and how fast they step out of it. It comes from the deck's Mana and Politics ratings plus how quick the hero is on their feet. It never guarantees a dodge: the reaction chance has diminishing returns (tops out near 65%), reactions can come late, and a step can come up short. In testing, heroes avoid a hit aimed right at them roughly 30–45% of the time.

🎒 Crypt Crawl: loadouts, a backpack, and summons with personality

  • Each hero has ability slots (2, then 3 at hero level 5, 4 at level 12), passive slots (1, then 2 at level 8) and 2 item slots. New picks that don't fit go into a shared 6-space backpack; at camp you can move things between the backpack and each hero (skills stay with the hero whose deck they came from; items fit anyone). Bagged gear can still roll upgrades.
  • Parties start with 2 heroes. The first time a save clears stage 6 you free a mystery stranger from the castle cells: pick which of your other heroes it turns out to be, they join the run right away (with 2 bonus upgrades), and that save can bring 3 heroes from then on.
  • Summons: melee summons hang about 3/4 across the screen and charge in; ranged summons hold the middle and shoot. Early summons make one creature and only one per ability is out at a time; higher ranks allow two, then three. Each hero's summon behaves differently on recast: Empower (grows the one out), Mend (heals and refreshes it), Volatile (the old one explodes), Swarm (two smaller ones), or Linger (lasts 18s).
  • Shots leave from each hero's weapon (bow hand, crossbow, staff orb, cannon, breath) in time with the strike frame. Hero cards say which deck inspired them.

🏃 Crypt Crawl: walking speeds, bigger hordes, and saves that survive updates

  • Heroes walk at their own pace (stone and armor slow, rogues and archers quick): fast ones drift to the front while marching and slow ones lag a little; the party's pace is the team average. Summons sprint ahead to meet monsters before the line and hold them up.
  • About 50% more monsters, mostly melee (a few fewer archers/casters), each a bit squishier and worth about a third less XP. Monsters now arrive as you advance, with only a trickle while you're held up; long stalls make monsters (and bosses after 90s) grow fiercer so fights always end.
  • The scout patrols wider and faster and pounces more often; Brick Toss no longer knocks back but stuns for 0.75s on a 7s cooldown.
  • Saves carry over game updates: hero levels and bests always stay; a run in progress keeps its spells/items, and anything that was changed or removed is swapped for the closest match at the same rank.

🏹 Crypt Crawl: slower, bigger shots and real ability names

  • Ranged heroes and casters fire about a quarter slower, and every projectile flies slower and is drawn bigger: real arrows, glowing orbs, ice spikes, crystal shards, plasma, lit shells. Multi-shot abilities fire fewer shots, spaced out (Volley 3 arrows, Shard Storm 2 shards, Mortar 2 shells).
  • Spells now have ability names themed on each deck (Grave Smite, Storm Burst, Forge Barrier, Glacial Grip…) instead of creature names; the card that inspired each one shows underneath. Items keep their card names.

🔍 Crypt Crawl: double-detail art, a roaming scout, and depth

  • All heroes, monsters and bosses now render at double resolution, so faces, belts, straps, pouches, quivers and boot cuffs show up.
  • The Spore Runners' scout is now a companion: she can't be targeted, roams around her partner shooting her bow, now and then pounces onto the front enemy with a knife, and lobs Brick Toss as their signature. She's drawn shorter and he's a bit taller.
  • Monsters stand on slightly different depth lanes, so they don't stack perfectly on top of each other; small creatures take the front lanes.

🗡️ Crypt Crawl: sharper heroes and partners that fight on their own

  • Every hero and monster was redrawn: more natural proportions, clean three-tone shading with crisp outlines, and new idle, flinch-when-hit and fallen frames (fallen heroes stay on the field, slain monsters drop before fading). Melee swings leave a crescent trail.
  • Every hero now has a built-in ⚡ signature ability on its own cooldown (Royal Cleave, Shield Wall, Rocket Hammer, Volley, Brick Toss, Blizzard…), cast automatically like everything else. The Spore Runners' scout now shoots a bow; the brick is their signature. A ↺ button restarts the current stage from its save point.
  • Partner decks are now two fighters with their own attacks: the ranged partner keeps throwing or casting at range while the melee partner only swings when something is in reach.

🔑 Crypt Crawl: PIN reset + six new monsters

  • Kyle's saves screen has a PIN reset: it clears a player's PIN on that device (their saves stay) so they can pick a new one. New enemies: ghouls and skull-throwing cultists in the graveyard, haunted knights (armored) and wolfmen in the castle, leeches and bog hags in the abbey.

⚰️ Crypt Crawl: a side-scrolling auto-battler

  • A pixel strip above the tabs shows a party marching through the crypt; tap ▶ PLAY CRYPT CRAWL to open the full game (works on phones, with a full-screen button).
  • Each player (🎩 Kyle, 🧀 Cheez, 🪼 Leon) has a 4-digit PIN and 3 save slots. Pick up to 3 heroes from your own decks; each deck is an original pixel hero built from its theme, partners fight as a duo, and stats come from the deck's ratings.
  • Heroes walk and fight on their own. Between stages you camp at a save point, spend level-ups (pick 1 of 3: new spells, items, upgrades or augments, rolled Common / Uncommon / Rare), then press Begin. Spells and items are named for real cards in that deck; about half the items carry a "chance on…" or triggered effect.
  • Three biomes (Hollowmere Graveyard, Castle Sanguine, The Drowned Abbey), a boss every third stage, 9 stages, then Prestige to loop with tougher monsters. Hero levels stay with the save (with catch-up XP); the run's loadout is lost when the party falls. Heavy hits knock enemies back.

🌕 A creepier night sky

  • The header's green orb is now a pixel-art moon with dithered craters and a sickly glow, ragged clouds drifting across it, a dead branch clawing in from the corner, pixel bats with red eyes flapping across the sky, and rolling ground fog along the bottom.

😬 Real status-bar faces in the life tracker

  • Each life panel now uses the classic status-bar face sprites: five rows from healthy to beat up as life drops, forward-facing faces show how healthy you are and keep looking around on their own; taking damage snaps the head to the side (plus a shocked face on a big hit: 10 at once, or 5+ in a burst); gaining life grins; at 0 life each knocked-out player gets their own death face, in order: skull and crossbones, pile of bones, rotting zombie, half skull, then a tombstone (Reset starts the order over).

💀 A meaner skeleton

  • The corner skeleton got redrawn: a real skull with glowing green eye sockets and a hat, a red bandana, an open duster coat over the ribs and spine, bony hands, jeans and boots, on a wooden chair. Same routine: a long drag with a glowing tip, smoke puffs and a ring, head bobbing to the music, then rocking back and tapping his boot.

🃏 Who goes first?

  • The life tracker has a 🃏 Who goes first? button: one face-down card is dealt to every player from a stack of Treasure tokens (real Treasure token art) plus one Piss Boy. The cards flip, and whoever drew Piss Boy goes first: their panel glows, gets a bouncing crown, a big PISS BOYYYY! banner, a party-popper and party-horn sound (if sound is on) and a burst of confetti.

⚰️ The Crypt + a life tracker

  • The Spinner page is now The Crypt: a tab for each player (🎩 Kyle, 🧀 Cheez, 🪼 Leon, and any new player automatically) with their haunted deck wheel (jack-o'-lantern hub, bone pointer, flickering candle lights, bats on the result), a short write-up of how they play, a 3D coin flip (🎃 heads / 💀 tails) and a dice roller: D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D20 and D%, 1-12 at a time, as tumbling bone dice (the D6 has skull pips).
  • 🎃 INSERT COIN at the top now opens a life tracker: 3-6 players, everyone starts at 40, big −10 / −1 / +1 / +10 buttons, a running +/− tally, tap a name to rename it, ⇅ to flip a panel for the player across the table, a full-screen button for phones, and it remembers the game if you close it. Each panel has a pixel-art status-bar face that gets bruised and bloodied as life drops, winces when hit, grins when healed, glances around, and turns into a grey skull at 0.
  • A chill skeleton in shades and a leather jacket kicks back in his chair: in the left margin on wide screens, in the header corner on smaller ones (never over the charts). He takes a drag, blows smoke rings, bobs his head to the music, then rocks the chair and taps his foot.

🎲 Pod Sim endings come from 306,000 simulated games

  • Every possible pod of four (3,060 of them) was played 100 times with the real decklists by a card-level engine: lands, ramp, commanders and tax, casting by mana value, Equipment paying its equip cost (or not, with Bruenor or Kíli), removal and wipes, combat with blocks, and commander damage.
  • Each pod keeps its most common outcomes (who wins, who falls in what order, who knocks them out, on which turn), up to seven per pod. PLAY picks one at random, more likely the more often it happened, and never the same one twice in a row; the story lines are re-rolled every time too. The ending says how often it came up.
  • The engine is rough (it loves Felothar's walls and Depala's Equipment, and undersells The Grim Throne's cheats and House on Haunted Hill's doors), so each winner's chance is scaled so the deck's overall win rate leans toward what its rating says. Matchups still come from the sims.
  • The ending-number buttons are gone: it's a new game every press.

📐 Rules 0.10.19: blue ratings in every stat

  • Every stat (except Mana, which keeps its fixed divide of 4) now rates against the second-best deck = 11, so the top one or two decks in each stat show up blue (10+). Totals rise 1.5–5 points: Grim 70 → 75, Vile Smashing 65.5 → 68.5, Felothar 65.5 → 68, Kykar 61 → 66.5.
  • "Me" is now Kyle everywhere on the site (🎩 Kyle on the spinner and the Show filter).

📜 Pod Sim: story mode with five endings per pod

  • The sim now tells the game as a story built from hand-written lines for all 18 decks: their real early plays (cheap rocks, dorks and 1-3 drops), mid-game commanders and engines at the right mana, removal aimed at each other's key cards, deck-vs-deck moments (one-sided wipes vs. tokens, fliers over walls, life swaps on a lifegain deck...), and finishers.
  • Each game runs as an Early game rundown (turns 1-3), a Mid game rundown (turns 4+), then the last three turns played out: swings, blocks, saves, knockouts and the final blow, with an ending title (Flawless Sweep, Comeback, Commander Damage, Speed Run, Last One Standing, Photo Finish).
  • Every pod of four (3,060 of them) has five endings of its own: always the same five for the same four decks, with different winners and stories. Pick 1-5, press PLAY for a random one, or 📜 ALL 5 ENDINGS to see who wins each.
  • No duplicates: picking the same deck twice blasts the screen with old-TV static and swaps one of the copies for a random deck not in the pod.

🦇 Blood Suckers: Bats are off the chopping block

  • Needs Repair never lists a Bat, or a card that makes or cares about Bats, for Blood Suckers. The five picks now are Campaign of Vengeance, Epicure of Blood, Path of Bravery, Diresight and Fracture, each with a budget and an any-cost swap.

🎃 Spooky retro theme

  • The site goes Castlevania × Halloween: acid-wash green and blood red on a midnight stone background, a gothic title, a glowing green moon, flapping bats, a jack-o'-lantern and candles, plus pumpkin, poison-green and violet spinner wheels. The pixel font, scanlines and CRT screen stay.

🕹️ Pod Sim plays real Magic now + 8-bit wheels

  • The sim now shuffles each deck's real list (lands, spells and commanders) and plays it turn by turn: a 7-card opening hand with a free mulligan for 0–1 or 6–7 lands, one land a turn, ramp adding mana, and spells cast only when you can pay their mana value. Commanders come down when affordable, go back to the command zone when removed and cost 2 more each time (commander tax).
  • Creatures have summoning sickness and can't attack the turn they land. Vehicles need crew. Evasion gets damage through, blockers trade or chump, and 21 commander damage knocks a player out. Removal goes after the biggest threat or a commander. Wipes only come out when you're behind (one-sided wipes like Slaughter the Strong keep your own board). Extra combats, damage doublers and overruns work like they should, and Felothar's walls hit for their toughness.
  • Every seat has a 🎲 die to roll a random deck, plus a dropdown to pick one. 🎲 ROLL ALL 4 rerolls the whole pod.
  • The spinner wheels went 8-bit: neon slices with black outlines, pixel lettering, square marquee lights, a pixel pointer and a SPIN button.

📐 New page: Stat Breakdown

  • One tab per stat (plus Ratings math): what it measures, every card formula written out, the deck-level checks, how the rating is worked out, and the whole pod's standings in that stat. Click any deck to open it.
  • Needs Repair now only lists cards worth replacing (no more "keep"), and each one has two swaps: 💰 a budget pick and 💎 an any-cost pick, all in the deck's colors and not already in the list.

🗡️ Rules 0.10.16: pump Equipment and Auras (Suit Up)

  • New pump formula for Equipment and Auras that boost one creature. Threats: Board Power on that creature (double strike or power doubling adds its power again). Equipment loses 0.05 per equip mana above 2, but gets +0.15 Survival because it moves to the next creature. Auras count x0.8 (removal takes both cards) unless they protect themselves (Rancor, Demonic Embrace).
  • Finish (Suit Up): when one suited-up creature hits for 6+, the card is also a finisher (x0.5 since it still has to connect). The carrier's power is the deck's usual one: 3 by default, 4 for Depala's pumped Dwarves and Felothar's walls, 5 for Kotis.
  • Suit-up stack (deck check): 4+ pump Equipment/Auras plus double strike sources add +0.25 Finish per double strike card (max 6). Free equips: decks with Bruenor, Kíli or other equip-cost cutters get the equip penalty back.
  • Finish bar lowered a bit (second-best deck = 11) as the new finishers join.
  • Moves: Tame Depala 55 → 62 (Finish 1 → 7, #14 → #6), Armed Robbery 53 → 60.5 (Finish 4 → 11), Felothar 64.5 → 65.5. Most others dropped 1–2 points since the Finish bar moved.

🕹️ New look + Pod Sim

  • The whole site got an 8-bit acid-punk arcade skin: pixel font, neon acid green / hot pink / cyan, pixel grid, CRT scanlines and a glitching title.
  • Pod Sim page: pick four decks (or roll a random pod), press PLAY, and watch a made-up game play out turn by turn on a CRT screen, built from each deck's ratings, key cards, commander and win plans. Endings change every run: Flawless Sweep, Comeback, Speed Run, Last One Standing or Time Called. RUN 1,000 GAMES shows who wins most often (seats shuffled). It's a rough model for fun, not a real game engine.

🎡 New page: Deck Spinner

  • One game-show wheel per player, one slice per deck they've added (equal odds). Hit SPIN in the middle of a wheel, or 🎰 SPIN EVERYONE to pick the whole pod's next game at once. New players get a wheel automatically when their first deck goes up.
  • New Show filter above the ratings: All decks, 🎩 Kyle, 🧀 Cheez or 🪼 Leon. It filters the ratings table and the deck tabs (ranks stay pod-wide).

🧱 Four new decks: Felothar, Thranduil 🪼, A Vile Smashing, Tame Depala

  • 🧪 A Vile Smashing (Ishai + Vial Smasher wheels and burn) lands at 66.5, #2 of 18: huge card flow from the wheels, plenty of edicts and wipes.
  • 🧱 Felothar (Abzan walls that hit for toughness) is 64.5, #4: Survival is maxed out from all the recursion, and the power-based wipes are one-sided because the walls have 0 power. On walls, Threats are scored on toughness.
  • 🧝 Thranduil 🪼 (Leon's Sultai Elves) is 56.5, #9: top-tier Mana from the Elf dorks, but Reach is 1 (no evasion) and removal is low.
  • ⚒️ Tame Depala (Boros Dwarves, Vehicles and Equipment) is 55.0, #14: strong Threats and Consistency, weak Cards and Mana, and creature removal is low.
  • Each deck got every card's text saved, full tags, Plan Tags (C/T) and synergy groups, two review passes, a Takeaway, land notes and Needs Repair picks with swap ideas.
  • Because ratings are relative, adding four decks moved the divides: the old decks dropped about 1–4 points each (Grim 74.5 → 71, Thing 68.5 → 65.5).

🔍 Tag audit: every deck, tag by tag

  • Checked all 14 decks one tag at a time (ramp, draw, tutors, selection, answers, survival, drain, politics, finish, tokens, team pumps, second life, evasion), matching each card's saved text against its tags. 29 missed tags added; everything else the check flagged was reviewed and is already covered.
  • Evasion on creatures that had none: Thrakkus, Ghostly Dancers, Knight of Dusk's Shadow, H.E.R.B.I.E. Scout Unit, Crystal, Cadira, Rat King, Ray Fillet, Ice-Fang Coatl.
  • Answers: Niv-Mizzet's pings, Goblin Bombardment (Last of Us and Korvold) and Judith can also kill small creatures.
  • Survival: Walking Skyscraper's hexproof (Mech and Primary Directive), Carnage Tyrant's hexproof, Galactus's indestructible, Stormbreath's protection, Gate Colossus coming back.
  • Politics: gift cards (Crumb and Get It, Starfall Invocation) and Skyline Despot's monarch.
  • Finish: Human Torch spreading his damage to every opponent, The Incredible Hulk's extra combats. Team counters: Unbreakable Formation's addendum (Blood Suckers and Kykar). Plus Lunar Convocation's Bats, Lessons from Life's land drop and Level Up's draw.
  • Totals that moved: Thing 66.5 → 68.5, Turtle 58 → 60.5, Double Dragons 65 → 66, Blood Suckers 55 → 56, Ominous Weather 52 → 53.

🤖 New deck: Primary Directive 🪼 (Leon's Optimus Prime robots)

  • Leon's Jeskai robot deck joins at 59 (#8 of 14). Leon's decks are marked with 🪼.
  • Cut from the 116-card list to 100, keeping robots first (by artwork), at least 15 ramp and 15 draw, every Iron Man, Master Transmuter, Braided Net, Kappa Cannoneer, all +2/+2 anthems, all recursion, Edgar, Shimmer Dragon, Insight Engine, Promise of Loyalty and Etherium Sculptor. Cuts: Single Combat, Solar Blaze, Page, Loose Leaf, Loreseeker's Stone, Flux Channeler, Ray Fillet, Wave Warrior, Season of Weaving, Wizard's Staff, The Everflowing Well // The Myriad Pools, Clay-Fired Bricks // Cosmium Kiln, Reality Heist, Sentry Bot, Super-Adaptoid, Vision, Spectral Synthezoid, Vulshok Factory, Thopter Shop.
  • 76 new cards saved with full text, tagged, Plan-Tagged (C = artifact creatures and counters for Optimus to bolster, T = the artifact engine) and grouped (Robots & artifact creatures, artifact payoffs, counters, Iron Man suits), then reviewed until a pass needed no changes.
  • Flags: removal is low (seven cards, counting Promise of Loyalty), and 8 lands enter tapped.

📈 Rules 0.10.14: Boosts for the lower decks

  • Vehicles dodge creature wipes (all decks): every Vehicle gets +0.15 Survival. Mechanized Mayhem runs 18: Survival 2 → 5, total 53 → 56.
  • Alpha-strike enablers count as Finish: tapping every blocker (Cone of Cold, Sleep, Icy Blast) and overruns (Become the Avalanche) are one-turn lethal setups. Ominous Weather's Finish 1 → 4, total 49 → 52.
  • Chandra's Ignition now also counts as a Finish in Korvold (a huge Korvold hits each opponent for his power): Finish 3 → 4, total 57 → 58.
  • Air density multiplier 0.40 → 0.60: Blood Suckers' Threats 4 → 5, total 54 → 55.
  • None of the top seven decks moved.

🗡️ Rules 0.10.13: Threats bar a smidgen lower

  • The Threats "10" is now set at the second-best deck's points ÷ 10.5 (was ÷ 10), so every deck needs about 5% fewer points per rating point.
  • Moved: Grim 73.5 → 74.5 (Threats 9 → 10), Thing 65.5 → 66.5, Double Dragons 64.5 → 65 (Threats 11 → 12), Mechanized Mayhem 52 → 53. Everyone else stayed put.

🐲 Rules 0.10.12: Big threats and copy engines

  • Tall threats: the mana penalty is now −0.08 per mana above 3 (was −0.10 per mana above 1). A 4/4 flier for 6 went from 0.15 to 0.41; a 12-power fatty for 7 went from 1.25 to 1.53. Big creatures count for more across the pod, so the deck that sets the Threats "10" moved too.
  • Commander copy engine (all decks): if the commander makes a token copy of each creature of a kind that enters, those creatures (its Plan Tag C cards) count their Tall threat ×1.5. Today that's Miirym: every Dragon comes in twice. Double Dragons' Threats 9 → 11.
  • Fixed three missing Tall tags in Double Dragons: Kura, Lozhan and Draconic Muralists.
  • Totals that moved: The Grim Throne 74.5 → 73.5 · Kykar, Zada & Feather 69 → 67 · Truly Fantastic 67.5 → 65.5 · Double Dragons 65 → 64.5 · House on Haunted Hill 61.5 → 59.5 · The Last of Us 60 → 59 · Turtle Power 59 → 58 · Armed Robbery 57 → 56 · Blood Suckers 55 → 54 · Mechanized Mayhem 55 → 52 · Ominous Weather 50 → 49. Card rankings, best/weakest cards and Needs Repair picks were all recomputed.

🦇 Rules 0.10.11: Quick Air

  • Small evasive creatures (too small to count as a Tall threat) now add to Threats: +0.10, +0.05 per power (up to 3), and +0.10 for each mana under 3. A 1-mana 1/1 flier gets +0.35; a 3-mana 2/2 flier gets +0.20.
  • Air density (deck check): Threats + 0.40 × (number of small evasive creatures ÷ their average mana value; 0.60 since 0.10.14). Lots of cheap fliers come out in bunches: Blood Suckers' 25 at an average of 2.8 mana gets +3.5; a deck with 4 at 4.5 mana gets +0.4.
  • Biggest change: Blood Suckers' Threats 3 → 5. Double Dragons and Mechanized Mayhem go 8 → 9; everyone else moves a fraction.

❄️🦇🐲🐉 Rules 0.10.10: Four new decks + Needs Repair fixes

  • New decks: Ominous Weather ❄️ (Isu snow tap-down, 50), Blood Suckers 🦇 🧀 (Zoraline Bat lifedrain, 53), Double Dragons 🐲 🧀 (Miirym Dragon copies, 64) and Korvold Eats Everything 🐉 🧀 (Korvold sacrifice, 57). That's 13 decks.
  • 227 new cards saved with their full text, then tagged, Plan-Tagged (C/T) and grouped, then reviewed card by card until a pass needed no changes. Each deck has its own synergy groups: snow permanents and tap-downs; Bats and life-gain drains; Dragons and Dragon payoffs; sacrifice outlets, death payoffs and tokens.
  • Snow-Covered basics now count as basic lands.
  • Needs Repair in the Garage now gives a 🛠️ Fix for every card it shows: a swap that fits the deck's colors and plan, or a reason to keep it.
  • With 13 decks, the second-best deck in each stat (which sets "10") changed, so the old decks moved a little: Grim 74.5, Kykar 69, Thing 67.5.

👑 Rules 0.10.9: Commander engines

  • A cheat effect on a commander (or secret commander) is the deck's planned strategy and always on hand, so it now counts toward Consistency instead of Mana. This applies to every deck. Right now it moves Dr. Eggman's free drops and Marina Vendrell's ETB.
  • Cheats now carry odds: 100% when you decide, 50% when an opponent picks (villainous choices, punishers). The value is scaled by the odds.
  • A commander cheat that repeats every turn also boosts Hit-Rate: every card it can put into play (its Plan Tag C cards) gets +0.5 × odds extra weight. Eggman (repeats every turn, 50%) gives +0.25 to each Robot, Construct and Vehicle.
  • Changes: Mechanized Mayhem Mana 10 → 7, Consistency 8 → 9, Threats 7 → 8, total 54 → 56. House on Haunted Hill Mana 12 → 11, Consistency 8 → 9, total 63 → 63.5.

🔗 Rules 0.10.8: Synergy groups

  • Each deck has 3–5 synergy groups, both creature types and non-creature themes (e.g. Grim: craft types, huge creatures, graveyard; Thing: noncreature spells, counters, extra combats, spell payoffs, trigger copiers, extra-draw package; Marina: Rooms, Curses, enchantment payoffs, Spirits; Mech: Robots & Constructs, Vehicles, artifact payoffs; Kotis: auras & equipment, mutate, combat-damage triggers, casting opponents' cards; Joel: Fungus & Saprolings, death triggers, sac outlets; Turtle: tokens, counters, Food, Ninjas & Turtles; Kykar: instants & sorceries, spell payoffs, spells that target your own creature, fliers; Mathas: life payment, life swaps, bounty, pillowfort).
  • Every card in a group gets a tiny bonus: +0.005 per other card in the group, max +0.15 per group, max 2 groups per card. Each group pays into the stat where it lands (types and tokens → Threats, death triggers → Reach, Curses and pillowfort → Politics, Rooms and enchantress → Cards, artifact payoffs → Mana…).
  • Then every deck got two more card-by-card passes over Plan Tags and group fits: fixes include Silver Surfer (finds Galactus), Condemn and the wipes for Mathas's bounties, Enchantress's Presence and Sanctum Weaver as enchantress cards, Felix and Baleful Eidolon for Kotis, Rites of Flourishing in Thing's extra-draw package, and Aqueous Form's scry cut down (it was over-scored).

🧩 Rules 0.10.7: Plan Tag

  • Plan Tag replaces Feeds the Plan and the hand-picked plan lists. Every card is checked from its own text: C = works alongside the commander (Robots, Constructs and Vehicles for Dr. Eggman; Dinosaurs, Merfolk, Pirates, Vampires and changelings for The Grim Captain; noncreature spells for The Thing and Kykar; auras and equipment for Kotis; tokens for Leonardo and Joel; bounty and removal for Mathas; Rooms and enchantments for Marina). T = fits the deck's main plan beyond the commander (big-creature cheat, spell payoffs, life as a resource, enchantress and Curses, artifact payoffs, mutate, aristocrat drains, go-wide pumps, spellslinger pings).
  • Card value: +0.15 (or +0.25 if it does it every turn), +0.05 more with both tags. It goes where the synergy really lands, often a weak stat: The Thing's spells → Threats, Kykar's spells → Mana (Spirits sacrifice for red), Kotis's gear → Threats, Eggman's Robots → Mana (free to put in), Joel's tokens → Cards and the drain pile → Reach, Mathas's bounties → Cards. Otherwise the card's best stat.
  • Hit-Rate now uses the tags: both tags 1, one tag 0.5, plus tutors and selection; 3 × the odds of seeing two in your first 10 cards + 1 × the odds of three.
  • Plan B counts T-tagged cards (they work without the commander): 1.5 × the odds of seeing two in 10 cards.
  • Swing's mana penalty is now −0.07 per mana above 3.

🔄 Rules 0.10.6: Swing Factor

New Swing tag in Threats for cards that can suddenly flip the standing of a game: Small (one player's spot flips) 0.25, Medium (a player's life or board turns around) 0.5, Large (the whole table resets) 0.75; +0.5 if repeatable, +0.25 at instant speed, −0.05 per mana above 3 (−0.07 from 0.10.7). Examples: Axis of Mortality and Soul Conduit (life swaps), Reverse the Sands, Tragic Arrogance, Quietus Spike, White Sun's Twilight, Rise and Shine. Life Swappin' Threats 1 → 3.

📖 Rules 0.10.5: full card-text review

Every card was re-read from its saved official text and missing tags were added. New: Rebound counts its free second cast at ×0.8 (Recurring Insight, Invisible Force Field, It's Clobberin' Time!). Biggest fixes: Sorcerer Class level 3 burns every opponent per spell, Secret Arcade turns every permanent into an enchantment for the enchantress engines, Tendershoot Dryad's city's blessing makes Saprolings 3/3, Tezzeret's Gatebreaker digs 5, Altar of the Wretched crafts a huge creature and comes back from the graveyard, Majestic Metamorphosis with Zada turns the team into 4/4 fliers, Jinnie Fay turns every token (even Food and Treasure) into a 2/2 or 3/1, plus Maskwood Nexus, Mirror Entity and Taurean Mauler now feed the Throne's craft. About 35 cards changed.

🎯 Rules 0.10.4: Hit-Rate, Plan B and token saturation

  • Plan cards: every deck has 16–22 hand-picked cards that make it do its thing (Grim's fatties and cheat engines, The Thing's draw engines, Mathas's swap pieces, Turtle's token engines…). Each one is also marked for how well it works without the commander.
  • Hit-Rate (Consistency): plan cards + tutors (+1 each) + selection cards (+0.5) + plan cards with Second Life (+0.25, you can use them twice). The odds of seeing at least one in your first 10 cards ×3, plus the odds of seeing two ×1.
  • Plan B (Consistency): the odds of seeing a plan card that still works without the commander, ×1.5.
  • Answer on time (Interaction): the odds of holding an answer by turn 4 (10 cards), +1 at 100%.
  • Closer on time (Finish): the odds of seeing a finisher by turn 7 (13 cards), +0.75 at 100%.
  • Fix: the Threat variety check now counts only real threat kinds (Tall, Wide, Board Power, noncreature threats, commander), not the new Body and Feeds the Plan bonuses.
  • Wide saturation (Threats): once a deck has 10 points of token makers, the rest count half. You can only cast so many token makers in a game. Turtle 15 → 13; Joel and Mech didn't move.

⚰️ Rules 0.10.3: Second Life (graveyard abilities)

Cards that do something again from the graveyard now score that second use: flashback, encore, recasting from the graveyard, and "exile this card from your graveyard" abilities that hand keywords or abilities to another creature. The graveyard effect is scored with the normal formulas at ×0.6 (it has to get there, and you pay again; ×0.4 if it also costs a card), plus 0.15 Cards for the extra use. Symbiote Spider-Man 0.29 → 1.18 (Find New Host gives its dig to a 12-power trampler), Scavenged Brawler 0.73 → 1.0, Seize the Day 0.65 → 1.25, Desperate Ravings 0.9 → 1.39.

🩸 Rules 0.10.2: bloodthirst and cheaper tutors (trial)

  • Bloodthirst creatures are scored at the size they usually enter: power + the counters (X = the deck's usual damage on its own turn), ×0.75 because you have to deal damage first. Indoraptor in the Grim Throne goes from 0.23 to 1.68 (counted as a 9-power menace).
  • Tutor cost penalty is now −0.25 per mana above 1 (was −0.5), on trial. Search for Glory 0.19 → 0.71, Micromancer 0 → 0.58, Buried Alive → 1.09.

🔧 Rules 0.10.1: lifting the weakest cards

  • Graveyard tutors: cards that put what you want into your graveyard (Buried Alive) now count like hand tutors, +0.25 for each extra card they find.
  • Feeds the Plan: +0.15 (or +0.25 if it happens every turn) when a card triggers the commander or a core engine, added to whatever that card is best at: cheap noncreature spells for The Thing and Kykar, tokens for Leonardo, tokens and bodies for Joel's drain, artifacts for Mech, enchantments for Marina, auras and equipment for Kotis, life payments for Mathas, and graveyard fuel for the Throne.
  • Body floor: a creature scoring under 0.5 now counts its body: a little Threats for its power and a little Survival for its toughness.
  • Later wipes are worth 60% of their value instead of losing a flat chunk.
  • Growers: creatures that grow every turn score at their grown size, like the other growers already did. Michelangelo went from 0.65 to 1.7: he grows each turn, has trample, and his Food token triggers Leonardo. Monastery Swiftspear, Frolicking Familiar, Crackdown Construct and Tempest Hart got the same fix.
  • Politics: single-target removal adds +0.10 (Direction: you choose who loses something, up to 8 cards), counterspells add +0.15 (Deals, up to 5), and the rating now uses the square root of Politics points. The low decks moved up (Kykar 1→6, Turtle 1→4) and Life Swappin' came down from 15 to 12.
  • Mana divide is fixed at 4.00 instead of following the second-highest deck, so more than one deck with heavy ramp can pass 10. Truly Fantastic, Marina and Turtle are now 10+.
  • 🔧 Needs Repair moved to the Garage and replaces the old "Weak spots & fixes" box. It picks each deck's five weakest links from three things at once: our score, how often EDHREC decks play the card, and my read of the card in that deck.

🔄 Rules 0.10: rebuilt from the ground up

Every old tag and score was thrown out. The pod is now these 9 decks, and every card was re-tagged with the new formulas over several review passes. Each formula starts from a small base value and adds or subtracts for things like mana value, instant speed, repeatable (engine) and conditions. Old totals aren't shown because the two systems don't compare.

🧮 How a rating is made

  • Each card's tags add points to one or more stats. Deck-level checks (below) add or subtract a little.
  • Divide number: in each stat, the second-highest deck is set to 10 and everyone else is scaled to match. A deck can go past 10 (max 15), but points above 10 count half in the group totals.
  • Groups: Engine (Mana, Cards, Consistency), Offense (Threats, Finish, Reach) and Defense (Interaction, Survival, Politics) are each out of 30. Total is out of 90.
  • Commanders score like any other card. There's no commander multiplier any more.

📐 The nine stats

  • ⚡ Mana: Ramp (lasting ×0.75, temporary ×0.5, +0.25 for putting a land out), Mana Boost, Cheat (skipping costs), Lands (only nonbasics with extra value score). Deck check: land count, how many lands enter untapped, color fixing, and a land-drop simulation.
  • 🃏 Cards: 0.25 base per card drawn, +0.75 for engines, −0.50 for "this turn only".
  • 🎯 Consistency: Tutors and card selection (scry, dig, loot), plus Hit-Rate (the odds of seeing your plan cards in your first 10 cards) and Plan B (the odds of seeing plan cards that still work without your commander).
  • 🗡️ Threats: Tall (big creatures, scaled by power and effective MV), Wide (tokens and engines), Board Power (anthems; capped at 20 boosted power so a single overrun can't explode). Deck check: threat variety.
  • 🏁 Finish (was Clock): cards that end games: bursts, extra combats, extra turns, alternate wins.
  • 🥷 Reach: evasion (flying, trample, unblockable) on your creatures, cards that give evasion, and drain/burn that skips combat.
  • ✨ Interaction: removal, counters, wipes and denial, all ×0.45. Modal cards score every mode. The first wipe in a deck scores full; later wipes count less. Deck check: does it answer creatures, artifacts, enchantments, planeswalkers, graveyards and spells?
  • 🔰 Survival: blockers, damage prevention, recursion, rebuilding and protection.
  • 🗣️ Politics: three levers, Deals (group hug, monarch, votes), Deterrents (taxes, pillowfort, punishers) and Direction (goad, redirecting). Decks that pull all three levers get a bonus; very salty decks get nudged down. Single-target removal and counterspells add a little, and the rating uses the square root of the points (0.10.1).

🤔 Calls I made while you were away

  • Divide = the second-highest deck in each stat, so one outlier deck can't squash everyone else.
  • Ratings are capped at 15, and Board Power is capped at 20 boosted power.
  • The commanders' text gets no multiplier; they score like any card.
  • New deck icons: 💰 Life Swappin', 🥚 Mechanized Mayhem, 🪶 Kykar, Zada & Feather.
  • X spells use a sensible X for each deck's mana (listed in each takeaway).

⚠️ Still to do

  • Kykar and The Last of Us are low on answers: fewer than 8 interaction cards each.
